name: Sun
notes: Reference origin. Adopted solar properties; NASA Sun facts and the IAU 2015 nominal effective temperature. Absolute visual magnitude +4.83: NASA Sun Fact Sheet (9 May 2024), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html . Solar reference: radius 1 R_sun = 695700 km (IAU 2015 B3); [M/H] = 0 dex by definition relative to the present Sun, not zero metal content; approximate formation age 4.6 Gyr (NASA Sun Facts). Mass and luminosity are unity in solar units; effective temperature 5772 K and spectral class G2V are adopted. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.07674 ; https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/ ; https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html ; https://www.sdss4.org/dr15/irspec/aspcap/ .

name: PSR J0437-4715 B
notes: Companion of PSR J0437-4715 in its 5.741-day orbit. Helium white dwarf seen in optical and infrared spectra; its hydrogen-atmosphere fit gives log g = 6.98 ± 0.15. Mass 0.221 ± 0.004 M_sun: Reardon et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07132. Effective temperature 3950 ± 150 K: Durant et al. 2012, https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.2346. Radius (1.9 ± 0.2) × 10^9 cm: Durant et al. 2012, https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.2346. Luminosity is derived from that radius and temperature. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 0.157 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference rhc+16). No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1012+5307 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1012+5307 in its 0.6047-day orbit. Low-mass helium-core white dwarf with Balmer absorption lines (DA; van Kerkwijk et al. 1996). Mass 0.165 ± 0.015 M_sun: Mata Sánchez et al. 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.02901. Effective temperature 8550 ± 25 K: van Kerkwijk et al. 1996, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9606045. Radius 0.047 ± 0.003 R_sun from photometry: Mata Sánchez et al. 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.02901. Luminosity is derived from that radius and temperature. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: Distance 877 pc (vlbi parallax): Ding et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.06351. Superseded: ATNF adopted distance 0.700 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference vwc+12). Replaces ATNF's 0.70 kpc (Verbiest et al. 2012); MSPSRpi Table 6 gives 0.877(35) kpc. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1614-2230 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1614-2230 in its 8.687-day orbit. Mass from the Shapiro delay; ATNF classifies the companion as a carbon–oxygen white dwarf. Mass 0.5 ± 0.006 M_sun: Demorest et al. 2010, https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.5788. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 0.700 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference mnf+16). No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J2222-0137 B
notes: Companion of PSR J2222-0137 in its 2.446-day orbit. Optical non-detection limits its effective temperature to below 3000 K (Kaplan et al. 2014, https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.0488), making it one of the coolest white dwarfs known. Mass 1.319 ± 0.004 M_sun: Guo et al. 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09474. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 0.269 kpc (parallax; reference ddfp24). No radial velocity is adopted.

name: Gaia BH1 B
notes: Companion of Gaia BH1 in its 185.4-day orbit. A slowly rotating, Sun-like G dwarf whose motion reveals the unseen black hole. Mass 0.93 ± 0.05 M_sun: El-Badry et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06833. Effective temperature 5850 ± 50 K: El-Badry et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06833. Radius 0.99 ± 0.05 R_sun: El-Badry et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06833. Luminosity 1.06 ± 0.04 L_sun: El-Badry et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06833. Metallicity [Fe/H] = -0.2 ± 0.05: El-Badry et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06833. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: El-Badry et al. 2023, Table 1 (Gaia DR3 orbital solution), https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06833; Nagarajan et al. 2024 systemic velocity; ~0.1 km/s ESPRESSO zero-point uncertainty, https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.05313.
astrometry_ref: El-Badry et al. 2023, Table 1 (Gaia DR3 orbital solution), https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06833
radial_velocity_ref: Nagarajan et al. 2024 systemic velocity; ~0.1 km/s ESPRESSO zero-point uncertainty, https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.05313

name: Gaia BH3 B
notes: Companion of Gaia BH3 in its 4253-day orbit. An old, very metal-poor giant of the Galactic halo (log g = 2.929 ± 0.003) whose motion reveals the unseen black hole. Mass 0.76 ± 0.05 M_sun: Gaia Collaboration 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10486. Effective temperature 5212 ± 80 K: Gaia Collaboration 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10486. Radius 4.936 ± 0.016 R_sun: Gaia Collaboration 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10486. Luminosity log(L/L_sun) = 1.208 ± 0.030: Gaia Collaboration 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10486. Metallicity [Fe/H] = -2.56 ± 0.11: Gaia Collaboration 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10486. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Gaia Collaboration 2024, Table 2 combined astrometric and spectroscopic solution, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10486; Gaia Collaboration 2024, Table 2 systemic velocity, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10486.
astrometry_ref: Gaia Collaboration 2024, Table 2 combined astrometric and spectroscopic solution, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10486
radial_velocity_ref: Gaia Collaboration 2024, Table 2 systemic velocity, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10486

name: Gaia NS1 B
notes: Companion of Gaia NS1 in its 731-day orbit. A lithium-rich, metal-poor halo star near the main-sequence turnoff. Its motion reveals the unseen neutron-star candidate. Temperature, radius, luminosity, mass and age are the paper's SED fit. Mass 0.79 ± 0.01 M_sun: El-Badry et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722. Effective temperature 5980 ± 55 K: El-Badry et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722. Radius 1.48 ± 0.05 R_sun: El-Badry et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722. Luminosity 2.51 ± 0.15 L_sun: El-Badry et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722. Metallicity [Fe/H] = -1.23 ± 0.08 from the spectroscopic fit: El-Badry et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722. Age 12.5 ± 0.5 Gyr: El-Badry et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: El-Badry et al. 2024, Table 3 Gaia + RV joint fit, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722; El-Badry et al. 2024, Table 3 systemic velocity, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722.
astrometry_ref: El-Badry et al. 2024, Table 3 Gaia + RV joint fit, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722
radial_velocity_ref: El-Badry et al. 2024, Table 3 systemic velocity, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06722

name: Gaia BH2 B
notes: Companion of Gaia BH2 in its 1277-day orbit. A low-luminosity, slightly metal-poor red giant enhanced in alpha elements; it reveals the unseen black hole through its orbit. Mass 1.19 ± 0.08 M_sun: Hey et al. 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09690. Effective temperature 4600 K: El-Badry et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.07880. Radius 7.8 R_sun: El-Badry et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.07880. Luminosity is derived from that radius and temperature. Metallicity [Fe/H] = -0.22: El-Badry et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.07880. Position is the unresolved system's: El-Badry et al. 2023. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: A0620-00 B
notes: Companion of A0620-00 in its 0.323-day orbit. A K-type donor star feeding the black hole; the 4600 K temperature is the value adopted in the mass analysis. Effective temperature 4600 K: van Grunsven et al. 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08209. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00211. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: XTE J1118+480 B
notes: Companion of XTE J1118+480 in its 0.17-day orbit. A cool dwarf donor; its K7 V to M1 V spectral type is from near-infrared spectroscopy (Khargharia et al. 2013, https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.2786). Position is the unresolved system's: SIMBAD. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: Cygnus X-1 B
notes: Companion of Cygnus X-1 in its 5.6-day orbit. The blue supergiant HDE 226868, whose wind feeds the black hole; the published mass interval is +7.7/-7.1 M_sun and the larger side is stored. Mass 40.6 ± 7.7 M_sun: Miller-Jones et al. 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09091. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00211. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: V404 Cygni B
notes: Companion of V404 Cygni in its 6.471-day orbit. A K-type giant losing gas to the black hole; its spectral type is from near-infrared spectroscopy (Khargharia et al. 2010, https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.5358). A wider third star also belongs to the system. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Parallax Miller-Jones et al. 2009, https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.5253; proper motion Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD. No radial velocity is adopted.
astrometry_ref: Parallax Miller-Jones et al. 2009, https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.5253; proper motion Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD

name: GRO J0422+32 B
notes: Companion of GRO J0422+32 in its 0.212-day orbit. A small M-type donor; its M1 spectral type is from Gelino & Harrison 2003, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0308490. Position is the unresolved system's: SIMBAD. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: GS 2000+25 B
notes: Companion of GS 2000+25 in its 0.3441-day orbit. A K-type dwarf donor, as listed by Casares & Jonker 2014, https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5118. Position is the unresolved system's: SIMBAD. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: MAXI J1820+070 B
notes: Companion of MAXI J1820+070 in its 0.6855-day orbit. A subgiant donor. Its temperature is about 4200 K at the system's distance; the published lower limit is 4200 K. Mass 0.49 ± 0.1 M_sun: Mikolajewska et al. 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.13201. Effective temperature 4200 K: Mikolajewska et al. 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.13201. Radius 1.19 ± 0.08 R_sun: Mikolajewska et al. 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.13201. Luminosity is derived from that radius and temperature. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Parallax Atri et al. 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.04525; proper motion Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD. No radial velocity is adopted.
astrometry_ref: Parallax Atri et al. 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.04525; proper motion Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD

name: Scorpius X-1 B
notes: Companion of Scorpius X-1 in its 0.7875-day orbit. A low-mass donor star, first caught through narrow emission lines from its X-ray-lit face (Steeghs & Casares 2002, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0107343). Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00211. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: Centaurus X-4 B
notes: Companion of Centaurus X-4 in its 0.6291-day orbit. A spotted K-type dwarf with 0.1755 times the neutron star's mass; K4 V and 4500 K are from González Hernández et al. 2005, as cited. Effective temperature 4500 K: Shahbaz et al. 2014, https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.1639. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00211. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: Vela X-1 B
notes: Companion of Vela X-1 in its 8.964-day orbit. The blue supergiant HD 77581, whose wind feeds the neutron star (Kretschmar et al. 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.13148). Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00211. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: X Persei B
notes: Companion of X Persei in its 250.5-day orbit. The Be star that gives the system its name. Its mass is the midpoint of the 13-20 M_sun range the source lists. Mass 16.5 ± 3.5 M_sun: Sanjurjo-Ferrín et al. 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09579. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00211. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: A0535+26 B
notes: Companion of A0535+26 in its 111-day orbit. A Be star whose gas disk feeds the neutron star's outbursts (Caballero et al. 2011, https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.3417); its spectral type is SIMBAD's. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00211. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: LS I +61 303 B
notes: Companion of LS I +61 303 in its 26.5-day orbit. A rapidly rotating B0 Ve star (Weng et al. 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.09423). Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00211. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: V404 Cygni C
notes: Companion of V404 Cygni. An evolved star at least 3,500 AU from the inner binary, 1.43 arcseconds away on the sky. Its evolved state dates the system to 3-5 Gyr; its plotted position is the system's. Its mass comes from isochrones. Mass about 1.2 M_sun: Burdge et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03719. Position and motion are the unresolved system's: Parallax Miller-Jones et al. 2009, https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.5253; proper motion Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD. No radial velocity is adopted.
astrometry_ref: Parallax Miller-Jones et al. 2009, https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.5253; proper motion Gaia DR3 via SIMBAD

name: PSR J1023+0038 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1023+0038 in its 0.1981-day orbit. A low-mass star that has fed the pulsar on and off; this is a transitional system moving between pulsar and X-ray binary states (Deller et al. 2012, https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.5670). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.190 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference sbc+21). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1024-0719 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1024-0719. A low-metallicity star on a very long orbit, published as 2,000 to 20,000 years. Mass about 0.4 M_sun: Kaplan et al. 2016, https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.00131. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: Distance 1080 pc (vlbi parallax): Ding et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.06351. Superseded: ATNF adopted distance 1.220 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference bjs+16). Replaces ATNF's 1.22 kpc (Bassa et al. 2016); MSPSRpi Table 6 gives 1.08(6) kpc. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J2129-0429 B
notes: Companion of PSR J2129-0429 in its 0.6352-day orbit. An optically bright redback companion with mean r-band magnitude 16.6 (Bellm et al. 2016, https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.00721). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.830 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference bkb+16). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1036-4353 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1036-4353 in its 0.2596-day orbit. A redback companion identified optically (Phosrisom et al. 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06503). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 0.408 kpc (dispersion measure model; reference ymw17). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1723-2837 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1723-2837 in its 0.6154-day orbit. An eclipsing redback companion. Its mass is the midpoint of the published 0.4-0.7 M_sun range. Mass 0.55 ± 0.15 M_sun: Crawford et al. 2013, https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.4956. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 0.926 kpc (parallax; reference jkc+18). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J2039-5617 B
notes: Companion of PSR J2039-5617 in its 0.228-day orbit. A redback companion with long-term optical variability (Clark et al. 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.14849). Its mass is the midpoint of the 0.15-0.22 M_sun range quoted. Mass 0.185 ± 0.035 M_sun: Zhang et al. 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17900. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.800 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference cnv+21). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1227-4853 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1227-4853 in its 0.2879-day orbit. The companion of a transitional redback pulsar (Johnson et al. 2015, https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.06862). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.613 kpc (parallax; reference jkc+18). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1740-5340A B
notes: Companion of PSR J1740-5340A in its 1.354-day orbit. A metal-poor “red straggler” in the globular cluster NGC 6397, from a high-resolution spectrum and Hubble photometry. Effective temperature 5410 ± 50 K: Orosz & van Kerkwijk 2003, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0210009. Radius 1.60 ± 0.17 R_sun: Orosz & van Kerkwijk 2003, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0210009. Luminosity is derived from that radius and temperature. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 2.482 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference bv21). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1740-5340B B
notes: Companion of PSR J1740-5340B in its 1.977-day orbit. A companion in NGC 6397 that has probably just left the main sequence and begun transferring mass (Zhang et al. 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07880). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 2.482 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference bv21). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1302-6350 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1302-6350 in its 1237-day orbit. The Be star LS 2883, oblate from fast rotation: its equator is near 27,500 K and its poles near 34,000 K, with an equatorial radius of 9.7 R_sun and a polar radius of 8.1 R_sun. Mass about 30.0 M_sun: Negueruela et al. 2011, https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.4636. Radius equatorial 9.7 R_sun: Negueruela et al. 2011, https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.4636. Luminosity log(L/L_sun) = 4.79: Negueruela et al. 2011, https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.4636. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 2.632 kpc (parallax; reference mds+18). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J2032+4127 B
notes: Companion of PSR J2032+4127 in its 1.68e+04-day orbit. The Be star MT91 213 in the Cygnus OB2 association. Mass about 15.0 M_sun: Lyne et al. 2015, https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.01465. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.330 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference kkv+15). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1431-4715 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1431-4715 in its 0.4497-day orbit. A redback companion, studied with optical spectroscopy (Strader et al. 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.04626). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.562 kpc (parallax; reference jkc+18). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J2339-0533 B
notes: Companion of PSR J2339-0533 in its 0.1931-day orbit. A strongly heated redback companion: its visible side varies from about 6900 K to below 3000 K across the orbit (Romani & Shaw 2011, https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.3074), and it has hot spots, likely magnetic poles, that move over the years (Kandel et al. 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.04105). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.100 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference rs11). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J0212+5321 B
notes: Companion of PSR J0212+5321 in its 0.8696-day orbit. An F6-type star tidally distorted by the pulsar; the type is Linares et al. 2017 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02232). The published mass interval is +0.22/-0.19 M_sun and the larger side is stored. Mass 0.5 ± 0.22 M_sun: Shahbaz et al. 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.07355. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 0.862 kpc (parallax; reference pbhg23). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J0838-2827 B
notes: Companion of PSR J0838-2827 in its 0.2145-day orbit. A heated companion of spectral type M1 or later (Halpern et al. 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.09511). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 0.413 kpc (dispersion measure model; reference ymw17). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J2302+4442 B
notes: Companion of PSR J2302+4442 in its 125.9-day orbit. A He- or CO-core white dwarf identified optically at r = 23.33. Published intervals are +0.25/-0.19 M_sun and +1000/-800 K; the larger sides are stored. Mass 0.52 ± 0.25 M_sun: Kirichenko et al. 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.09442. Effective temperature 6300 ± 1000 K: Kirichenko et al. 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.09442. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 0.859 kpc (dispersion measure model; reference ymw17). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J0337+1715 B
notes: Companion of PSR J0337+1715 in its 1.629-day orbit. The inner of the pulsar's two white dwarfs: hot and low-gravity, with log g = 5.82 ± 0.05. Its outer white dwarf has 0.40962 M_sun but no optical detection. Mass 0.1973 ± 4e-05 M_sun: Archibald et al. 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.02059. Effective temperature 15800 ± 100 K: Kaplan et al. 2014, https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.0407. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.300 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference kvk+14). No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1738+0333 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1738+0333 in its 0.3548-day orbit. A low-mass white dwarf with a thick hydrogen envelope, bright enough for spectroscopy. The published interval is +0.007/-0.005 M_sun and the larger side is stored. Mass 0.181 ± 0.007 M_sun: Antoniadis et al. 2012, https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.3948. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.695 kpc (parallax; reference dds+23). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J2317+1439 B
notes: Companion of PSR J2317+1439 in its 2.459-day orbit. A white dwarf with a cooling age of 10.9 ± 0.3 Gyr. Published intervals are +0.13/-0.10 M_sun and +550/-470 K; the larger sides are stored. Mass 0.39 ± 0.13 M_sun: Dai et al. 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02593. Effective temperature 8077 ± 550 K: Dai et al. 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02593. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.667 kpc (parallax; reference aab+21a). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1400-1431 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1400-1431 in its 9.547-day orbit. A cool DA white dwarf; its radius scales with the assumed distance. Mass about 0.3 M_sun: Swiggum et al. 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09386. Effective temperature 3000 ± 100 K: Swiggum et al. 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09386. Radius (2.19 ± 0.03) × 10^-2 R_sun at 270 pc: Swiggum et al. 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09386. Luminosity is derived from that radius and temperature. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 0.278 kpc (parallax; reference skm+17). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J1741+1351 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1741+1351 in its 16.34-day orbit. Probably a He-core white dwarf, matching the mass from radio timing. Mass about 0.2 M_sun: Zyuzin et al. 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.00331. Effective temperature 6000 K: Zyuzin et al. 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.00331. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.667 kpc (parallax; reference abb+18). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J0348+0432 B
notes: Companion of PSR J0348+0432 in its 0.1024-day orbit. A white dwarf with very low mass, whose spectroscopy set the system's mass ratio. Mass 0.154 ± 0.003 M_sun: Saffer et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.02850. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 2.100 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference afw+13). No radial velocity is adopted.

name: PSR J0023+0923 B
notes: Companion of PSR J0023+0923 in its 0.1388-day orbit. A black-widow companion: a very low-mass object heated by the pulsar and seen optically (Breton et al. 2013, https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.1790). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.818 kpc (parallax; reference aab+21a). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.

notes: Companion of PSR J0610-2100 in its 0.286-day orbit. Mass about 0.02 M_sun: Pallanca et al. 2012, https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6515. Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.389 kpc (parallax; reference dds+23). name: PSR J1959+2048 B
notes: Companion of PSR J1959+2048 in its 0.382-day orbit. The original black-widow companion, heated on its pulsar-facing side and cooler than about 2800 K on its far side (Fruchter et al. 1995, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9502084). The pulsar outweighs it 69.2 ± 0.8 times (van Kerkwijk et al. 2011, https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.5427). Position, parallax and proper motion are the pulsar system's: ATNF adopted distance 1.400 kpc (independent distance estimate; reference br14). Companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar and inclinations of 90 and 60 degrees. No radial velocity is adopted.
